meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 3: Server Features (Tools, Resources, Prompts)

questions.question: What are the three core primitives that MCP servers can expose?
questions.explanation: Servers expose Tools (executable functions), Resources (read-only data sources providing context), and Prompts (reusable interaction templates).

questions.question: Who 'controls' each server primitive according to the interaction model in the docs?

options.text: Tools: user, Resources: model, Prompts: application
Tools: model, Resources: application, Prompts: user
Tools: application, Resources: user, Prompts: model
All three are controlled by the model

questions.explanation: Tools are model-controlled (the LLM decides when to invoke them), resources are application-driven (the host decides how to retrieve and use them), and prompts are user-controlled (requiring explicit invocation, e.g., via slash commands).

questions.question: Which pair of protocol methods is used to discover and execute tools?
questions.explanation: Clients discover tools with tools/list (returning definitions with JSON Schemas) and execute a specific tool with tools/call.

questions.question: What schema language does MCP use to define and validate tool inputs?
questions.explanation: Each tool declares an inputSchema in JSON Schema, which enables type validation and documents required and optional parameters. Tools may also declare an optional outputSchema.

questions.question: How is a Resource uniquely identified in MCP?

options.text: By a sequential integer ID assigned by the client
By a unique URI, e.g., file:///path/to/document.md

questions.explanation: Each resource has a unique URI (such as file:///path/to/document.md) and declares its MIME type for appropriate content handling.

questions.question: What distinguishes a Resource Template from a Direct Resource?

options.text: Templates are write-enabled while direct resources are read-only
Templates use dynamic URIs with parameters (e.g., travel://activities/{city}/{category}) while direct resources have fixed URIs

questions.explanation: Direct resources are fixed URIs pointing to specific data; resource templates are dynamic URIs with parameters that enable flexible queries, discovered via resources/templates/list, and they support parameter completion.

questions.question: Which protocol method retrieves the full definition of a specific prompt, including its arguments?
questions.explanation: prompts/list discovers available prompts, and prompts/get retrieves a full prompt definition with its arguments.

questions.question: A client wants to be notified when a specific resource changes. How does it accomplish this in the 2026-07-28 protocol?

options.text: By calling resources/subscribe with the URI
By sending a subscriptions/listen request with the resource URIs listed in the resourceSubscriptions filter
By re-reading the resource on a timer; there is no notification mechanism
By setting watch: true in resources/read

questions.explanation: To watch resources, the client sends subscriptions/listen with the URIs in the resourceSubscriptions filter; the server delivers notifications/resources/updated on the resulting stream whenever a watched resource changes.

questions.question: In the tools/call response, tool output is returned in which structure?

options.text: A single plain string field named output
A content array of typed content objects (e.g., type: "text")

questions.explanation: Tool responses return a content array of content objects, each with a type field (text, images, resources, etc.), enabling rich multi-format responses.

questions.question: Which UI patterns do applications typically use to expose user-controlled prompts?

options.text: Slash commands, command palettes, dedicated buttons, and context menus
Only automatic invocation by the model
Hidden system prompts the user never sees

questions.explanation: Prompts require explicit invocation, and applications commonly expose them via slash commands (e.g., /plan-vacation), command palettes, dedicated UI buttons, and context menus.

questions.question: SCENARIO: You're building an MCP server for a database. You want to expose (a) a way to run queries, (b) the database schema for context, and (c) few-shot examples showing how to query well. Which primitives map to (a), (b), and (c)?
questions.explanation: This is the exact example from the architecture docs: a database server exposes tools for querying, a resource containing the schema, and a prompt with few-shot examples for interacting with the tools.

questions.question: SCENARIO: A tool is registered as 'calculate' on a server that may later add currency conversion and unit conversion tools. Following the naming guidance from the tool discovery docs, what should you do?

options.text: Use a clearer, namespaced-style name such as 'calculator_arithmetic' so the name uniquely and descriptively identifies the operation within the server's namespace
Use a random UUID as the name
Names don't matter because the title field is what the model sees

questions.explanation: The docs recommend names follow a clear naming pattern (e.g., calculator_arithmetic rather than just calculate). The name is the unique identifier and primary key for execution within the server's namespace, so descriptive, unambiguous names improve tool selection.

questions.question: SCENARIO: A user is filling in the {city} parameter of the resource template weather://forecast/{city}/{date} and types 'Par'. What MCP feature lets the application suggest 'Paris' or 'Park City'?

options.text: Parameter completion on resource templates (also supported by prompts)

questions.explanation: Dynamic resources support parameter completion: typing 'Par' can suggest 'Paris' or 'Park City', helping users discover valid values without knowing exact formats. Prompts support argument completion similarly.

questions.question: Which method discovers Resource Templates specifically (as opposed to direct resources)?
questions.explanation: resources/list returns direct resource descriptors, while resources/templates/list returns resource template definitions (uriTemplate, name, title, description, mimeType). resources/read retrieves contents.

questions.question: What human-oversight mechanisms do the docs suggest applications implement around model-controlled tools?

options.text: Approval dialogs for executions, permission settings for pre-approving safe operations, UI display of available tools, and activity logs of executions
A mandatory 24-hour delay before any tool runs

questions.explanation: Because tools are model-controlled, MCP emphasizes human oversight: showing available tools in the UI, approval dialogs for individual executions, permission settings for pre-approved safe operations, and activity logs showing executions with results.

questions.question: Which content block types can appear in a tool result's content array?

options.text: Text, images, audio, resource links, and embedded resources
Raw binary streams without type information

questions.explanation: Tool results are arrays of typed content blocks: text content, image content, audio content (both base64 with a mimeType), resource links (a URI reference without inline contents), and embedded resources (full resource contents inside the result).

questions.question: What's the difference between a resource link and an embedded resource in a tool result?

options.text: A resource link references a resource by URI without carrying its contents (the client may fetch it via resources/read); an embedded resource carries the full resource contents inline within the result
Resource links are only for images
Embedded resources must be fetched separately

questions.explanation: Links defer the payload — useful for large or optional data the client can read on demand; embedded resources inline the payload so no follow-up read is needed.

questions.question: How are binary payloads like images and audio carried in MCP content blocks?

options.text: As raw bytes appended after the JSON
Base64-encoded in the block's data field, accompanied by a mimeType so the client knows how to interpret them
As URLs only — binary data cannot travel inline
As hexadecimal strings in the params

questions.explanation: JSON-RPC is text-based, so image/audio content blocks carry base64 data plus a mimeType (e.g., image/png, audio/wav). Large binaries can alternatively be exposed as resources and referenced by link.

questions.question: During a conversation, the LLM decides on its own that calling get_weather would help answer the user, and the host shows an approval prompt before executing. Which primitive and control model is this?

options.text: A Tool - model-controlled, with human oversight via approval

questions.explanation: Tools are model-controlled: the LLM decides when to invoke them, while the host keeps a human in the loop (visibility, per-call approval, pre-approval settings, activity logs). (MCP docs, server concepts control model.)

questions.question: A host application automatically attaches the contents of file:///project/README.md to the model's context before a chat turn, without the model or the user asking. Which control model is exercised?

options.text: Model-controlled, because the content reaches the model
Application-controlled - Resources are retrieved and used at the host's discretion
User-controlled, because the user owns the file
Server-controlled, because the server exposes the URI

questions.explanation: Resources are application-driven: the host decides how and when to retrieve them and how to use them. Tools are model-controlled and Prompts are user-controlled - the classic Model->Tools, App->Resources, User->Prompts mapping. (MCP docs, server concepts.)

questions.question: A user types the /code-review slash command, which the client fetched from a server via prompts/list. Which control model does this demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Prompts are user-controlled templates: they require explicit user invocation, typically surfaced as slash commands or menu entries. (MCP docs, server concepts.)

questions.question: A tool's downstream API returns HTTP 500 while executing tools/call. What should the MCP server return?

options.text: A JSON-RPC error response with code -32603
A normal result (resultType "complete") whose payload sets isError: true and describes the failure
resultType "input_required" so the client can retry

questions.explanation: Tool *execution* failures are reported inside the result via isError: true, so the model can see and react to the failure. JSON-RPC errors are reserved for protocol-level problems (unknown tool, invalid params, server bugs). (MCP docs, tools; a classic exam trap.)

questions.question: Two different servers connected to the same host both expose a tool named search. Who is responsible for disambiguating?

options.text: The spec forbids connecting both servers simultaneously
Tool names must be globally unique across the ecosystem, so one server is non-compliant
Tool names are unique per server; handling cross-server collisions (e.g., prefixing) is the host's responsibility
The registry rejects duplicate tool names at publish time

questions.explanation: Uniqueness is scoped to a single server. When multiple servers collide, the host disambiguates - commonly by prefixing tool names with a server identifier. (MCP docs, server concepts.)

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the spec's Security and Trust key principles, stated correctly?

options.text: Tool descriptions and annotations are considered untrusted unless obtained from a trusted server
Servers must sandbox every tool in a container
Hosts may transmit resource data to third parties as long as it is encrypted
User consent is only required for write operations, not reads

questions.explanation: Under Tool Safety, tools represent arbitrary code execution and descriptions/annotations are untrusted unless from a trusted server. The other statements contradict the principles: hosts must not transmit resource data elsewhere without consent, and explicit consent covers all data access and operations. (Spec 2026-07-28 overview, Security and Trust.)

questions.question: Which method does the client use to discover available tools from a server?
questions.explanation: The tools/list method returns all available tools. tools/call is used to invoke a tool, not discover it.

questions.question: In the control model, Tools are considered 'DO' primitives because:

options.text: The model reads data from them
The model executes actions through them

questions.explanation: Tools are 'DO' primitives - the model decides to execute an action. Resources are 'IS' primitives - the model reads information.

questions.question: When the model decides to call a tool, what happens before execution?
questions.explanation: The host must obtain user consent before executing a tool. This is a key security principle - human-in-the-loop.

questions.question: A user asks the AI to 'read the README file and then fix the bug'. Which sequence of primitives is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Reading a file is a Resource (application-controlled, IS). Fixing a bug is a Tool (model-controlled, DO). The host decides which resources to include, then the model decides which tools to call.
